LOCALITY_NOTES: This area contains two separate midden sampling localities in Echo Canyon along Interstate 80, about 14km southwest from Castle Rock.  The first locality occurs near the Emory railroad siding (1.5km west of it), east of the confluence of Heiners Creek and Echo Creek, on a south-facing conglomerate cliff.  The second sampling locality in the lower Echo Canyon area is approx.. 3.3km northwest of the first locality (2km northeast of Emory) opposite the small tributary Stag Canyon.  This is a south-facing conglomerate cliff, with a thick grove of willows, oak, and sumac on the steep slope below.  Original location coordinates are given as Northing and Easting, the values on p. 26 are reversed, Northing 4543600 Easting 473046.

LOCALITY_NOTES: West of Topaz Lake, CA.  The midden site is 2km south of California State Highway 89, 4km SW of Topaz Lake, and in the Sierra Nevada.  Two midden subsamples were taken within 2 meters of each other.  They were moderately-welded, brecciated tuff at the top of a 20 degree slope, near the confluence of two washes, and had a NW aspect.  Midden 1 was on top of a ledge and underneath a rock overhang.  This midden was mostly protected from weather and had evidence of modern woodrat activity.

COMMENTS: Complete taxon list from Emslie et al., 2015 (317m).
LOCALITY_NOTES:
Site 1 (UR 1) was a series of exposed middens on a narrow cliff ledge at an elevation of 1575 meters. S1 was collected on 2 August 2006 in a seam in the rock 1 meter above the floor of the ledge at its midpoint. S2 was collected from the floor of the ledge near the north end. S3 was collected from the roof of an alcove below the ledge.
Analysis of S2 indicated that more midden material was required as the sample was dominated by geological matrix, and so it was resampled on 6 August 2008. During this resampling, the cliff base was surveyed to the south.
BEST_LOCALITY_NOTES: Used TOPO and 317m for best locality estimate.  We moved the point slightly to match the published elevation.

COMMENTS: Complete taxon list from Nowak, 1991 (326m).
LOCALITY_NOTES: East Fork of the Carson River near Markleeville, CA.  Midden site is .6km from California State Highway 4 and 9.5km SE of Markleeville.  An extensive midden along the cliffs of the East Carson River was subsamples.  This midden is unique in that it was within 10 meters of the river and was at the interface of a true riparian habitat and mixed conifer, montane forest.  The midden was in a solution hollow along a semi-vertical seam of an andesite tuff-breccia outcrop and was protected from weather.  The rock outcrop containing the midden lay at the west end of a 13 degree slope and had and easterly aspect.  Modern woodrat midden material was present.
BEST_LOCALITY_NOTES: Used TOPO and 326m for best localiity estimate.  Moved the location slightly to the published elevation, moved closer to the stream.

Catclaw acacia (Acacia greggii) and velvet mesquite (Prosopis juliflora var. velutina) are presently restricted to riparian environments along the Gila River and perhaps occasionally in Coyote Wash.
